chapter.title: Works of art, collectors' pieces and antiques

page.h1: HTS Chapter 97: Works of art, collectors' pieces and antiques — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Import Duty on U.S. Art: UK, EU, Switzerland, China and Hong Kong Rates | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Eight of the ten largest markets charge 0% on U.S. paintings, sculpture and antiques; China adds counter-tariffs. Rates and import rules by market.
keywords: import duty on art into uk
is there a tariff on art

intro: Eight of the ten largest markets — the **EU, the UK, Switzerland, Hong Kong, South Korea, Japan, Mexico and Canada** — charge **0%** on U.S. paintings, prints, sculpture, stamps, collections and antiques. **China** charges a low normal rate (0–6%) but adds its 2019 counter-tariffs (10–25%) and the 10% extra on all U.S. goods, so an original painting pays 31%; the **UAE** charges the 5% Gulf common tariff. With duty mostly at zero, access depends on each market’s rules for cultural property and protected wildlife, so each card names that authority. Import VAT and the buyer’s own paperwork are outside this page.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

markets.rule: EU common customs tariff: 0% on every Chapter 97 line

profile.headline: The largest market: $3.83B in 2025 (+7.5%), led by France ($1.30B), Germany ($608M), Italy ($404M), Belgium ($402M) and Luxembourg ($344M, +96%). Duty is 0%; for older cultural goods the importer needs an EU import licence or importer statement.
profile.mainProducts: Paintings, drawings, pastels, collages & mosaics (executed by hand) (9701) · Original sculptures & statuary, in any material (9703)
profile.tariffNow: Free (EU tariff 0% on all of Chapter 97)

regulator.name: Member-state competent authorities, through the EU’s ICG system (Regulation (EU) 2019/880)
regulator.requirement: Since June 28, 2025, archaeological objects and dismembered parts of monuments over 250 years old need an import licence, and paintings, prints, sculpture, collections and antiques over 200 years old worth €18,000 or more an importer statement, unless created or discovered in the EU. Proof of lawful export from the country of creation is needed, or from the last country of over five years’ stay for goods that left before April 24, 1972.

profile.headline: $2.36B in 2025 (+2.7%), the largest single buyer, and up 5.1% in January–August 2026. Paintings and drawings were $1.79B of it. The UK charges no duty on art; antiques containing ivory need an Ivory Act exemption.
profile.mainProducts: Paintings, drawings, pastels, collages & mosaics (executed by hand) (9701) · Original sculptures & statuary, in any material (9703)

regulator.name: Animal and Plant Health Agency (Ivory Act 2018)
regulator.requirement: Importing an item made of or containing elephant, hippo, killer whale, narwhal or sperm whale ivory to sell or hire needs a registered exemption (for example pre-1947 with under 10% ivory, or a pre-1918 portrait miniature) or an exemption certificate for a pre-1918 item of outstandingly high value.

profile.headline: $1.65B in 2025 (+5.0%), though January–August 2026 was down 23.1%. Paintings and drawings were $1.33B. Switzerland charges no duty, but cultural property must be declared as such at customs.

regulator.requirement: Cultural property must be declared as such and in detail at Swiss customs, including in a customs warehouse or free port; since the revised ordinance of January 1, 2026 the declaration gives the type, dating and dimensions of each object.

regulator.requirement: No import licence is needed for art in general; works made with CITES-listed species, such as ivory or tortoiseshell, need a CITES import permit from a regional environmental office.

markets.name: China
markets.rule: China’s MFN rates (0–6%) + 2019 counter-tariffs + 10% extra on all U.S. goods

9701.normalRate: 1–6% normal; 0% in 2026 on paintings over 100 years
9701.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 and 2026 interim rates (Announcements No. 12 and No. 11 of 2025): 1% on original paintings under 100 years (9701.9119), 6% on thangka, reproductions, mosaics and collages, 0% interim on paintings over 100 years (9701.21–29); 2019 counter-tariff 20% on original paintings other than thangka (Annex 2) and 10% on reproductions and collages (Annex 3) unless excluded; plus the 10% extra on all U.S. goods (Announcement No. 7 of 2025), 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027

9702.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 and 2026 interim rates (Announcements No. 12 and No. 11 of 2025): 1% for 9702.10 and 9702.90; 2019 counter-tariff 10% on original prints (Annex 3) unless excluded; plus the 10% extra on all U.S. goods (Announcement No. 7 of 2025), 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027

9703.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 and 2026 interim rates (Announcements No. 12 and No. 11 of 2025): 1% for 9703.10 and 9703.90; 2019 counter-tariff 20% on original sculpture (Annex 2) unless excluded; plus the 10% extra on all U.S. goods (Announcement No. 7 of 2025), 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027

9704.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 and 2026 interim rates (Announcements No. 12 and No. 11 of 2025): 4% on postage stamps (9704.0010), 6% on other items (9704.0090); 2019 counter-tariff 25% on postage stamps (Annex 1); the 10% on other items listed in 2019 was never applied; plus the 10% extra on all U.S. goods (Announcement No. 7 of 2025), 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027

9705.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 and 2026 interim rates (Announcements No. 12 and No. 11 of 2025): 0% for 9705.10–9705.39; 2019 counter-tariff 10% on collections and collectors’ pieces (Annex 3) unless excluded; plus the 10% extra on all U.S. goods (Announcement No. 7 of 2025), 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027

9706.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 and 2026 interim rates (Announcements No. 12 and No. 11 of 2025): 0% for 9706.10 and 9706.90; 2019 counter-tariff 20% on antiques over 100 years (Annex 2) unless excluded; plus the 10% extra on all U.S. goods (Announcement No. 7 of 2025), 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027

profile.headline: $124M in 2025 (−15.1%): $57M of paintings and $42M of antiques. The costliest large market: an original painting pays 31% and an antique 30%. Imported artworks for sale also need provincial approval.
profile.mainProducts: Paintings, drawings, pastels, collages & mosaics (executed by hand) (9701) · Antiques over 100 years old (9706)

regulator.name: Provincial departments of culture and tourism (Art Market Management Measures)
regulator.requirement: A business importing artworks must apply, before import, to the culture department of the province of the port of entry with its business licence, the works’ source and a catalogue; customs clears the works on the approval, and unapproved imports may not be sold (Articles 14 and 18).

markets.name: Canada
markets.rule: CUSMA: 0% on qualifying U.S. goods (Canada’s MFN is free on original works)

9701.basis: CUSMA; Canada Customs Tariff 2026: originals by artists free (9701.21.10, 9701.91.10 and similar), other hand-painted items 5.5–7%; 25% counter-tariff on 9701.91.10 from March 4 to September 1, 2025 (SOR/2025-66)

9702.basis: CUSMA; Canada Customs Tariff 2026: 9702.10.00 and 9702.90.00 free

9703.basis: CUSMA; Canada Customs Tariff 2026: 9703.10.00 and 9703.90.00 free

9704.basis: CUSMA; Canada Customs Tariff 2026 and WITS/TRAINS MFN applied rates, 2023: free

9705.basis: CUSMA; Canada Customs Tariff 2026 and WITS/TRAINS MFN applied rates, 2023: free

9706.basis: CUSMA; Canada Customs Tariff 2026: 9706.10.00 and 9706.90.00 free

profile.headline: $111M in 2025 (−12.2%). Original paintings, prints, sculpture and antiques are duty-free from any country; other hand-painted items are free only under CUSMA. Canada’s 25% counter-tariff on U.S. original paintings ended September 1, 2025.
profile.mainProducts: Paintings, drawings, pastels, collages & mosaics (executed by hand) (9701) · Original sculptures & statuary, in any material (9703)
profile.tariffNow: Free (CUSMA); 2025 counter-tariff on original paintings removed

regulator.name: Canada Border Services Agency (Cultural Property Export and Import Act)
regulator.requirement: No import permit is needed for art; it is illegal to import foreign cultural property illegally exported from a state that has a cultural property agreement with Canada (sections 37(2) and 43).

assumptions: Rates are what U.S.-origin goods pay in November 2026. MFN rates are the World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) applied rates for 2023 at the six-digit level, checked against the 2026 schedules of the UK, Japan, Canada and China and Mexico’s LIGIE.

China’s cells add three layers: its 2026 MFN or interim rate, the 2019 counter-tariffs (Annexes 1–3 of Tariff Commission Announcement No. 3 of 2019, charged unless the buyer holds an exclusion valid to December 31, 2026) and the 10% extra on all U.S. goods. The 2019 lists use 2017-edition lines (9701.1019, 9703.0000, 9706.0000 and so on), which cover the same goods.

Free-trade-agreement rates (KORUS, USMCA/CUSMA) apply to goods that meet the agreement’s rules of origin; the normal rate shows what other goods pay. For most of Chapter 97 the normal rate is already 0%.
Each heading’s cell is the rate on its main six-digit lines; where lines differ (China, Canada 9701) the basis gives each.
Import VAT and sales taxes, which several markets charge on art at import, are the buyer’s business and are not shown.
National 8- to 10-digit lines can differ from the six-digit rate shown.
